title: Grid-map superposition duplicates transverse fields on axis
summary: When a Cartesian grid precedes an axisymmetric grid in the same element, evaluating the field exactly on axis adds the first grid’s transverse field twice. Constant magnetic grids (0.7, −0.4, 0.2) T and (0, 0, 1.3) T return (1.4, −0.8, 1.5) T instead of their vector sum (0.7, −0.4, 1.5) T. Reversing the grid order, evaluating either grid alone, or moving off axis gives the correct result. The axisymmetric branch leaves transverse components from the preceding grid in its temporary accumulator.

title: Longitudinal IBS equilibrium balances RMS spread instead of variance
summary: Both IBS equilibrium solvers balance radiation damping against IBS growth using RMS energy spread instead of its variance. For amplitude damping time τ, RMS IBS growth rate r and zero-current RMS spread σ₀, equilibrium requires RMS spread σ = σ₀/√(1 − τr), with r evaluated self-consistently. The solvers instead use σ = σ₀/(1 − τr). In a 2 GeV electron case, the derivative solver returns relative energy spread 0.001221 instead of 0.001139, an excess of 7.241%; the relaxation solver gives the same erroneous balance.

summary: When the envelope radiation-diffusion helper is called for a heavier species, its classical radius changes with species but its recoil coefficient keeps the electron mass. title: Sequential step clipping violates earlier variable bounds
summary: `Line.match()` can accept an iteration that exceeds an earlier variable's `Vary.max_step`, because clipping a later variable rescales the already clipped step vector and enlarges it. title: Variable weights distort physical maximum steps
summary: Giving a matching variable a `weight` other than one changes its effective `max_step` in the variable's own units. title: Manager.copy disconnects containers from dependency tasks
summary: In Xdeps, the dependency-graph library behind Xtrack's deferred expressions, `Manager.copy` deep-copies the containers, the tasks (expressions computing dependent values) and the dependency maps separately, so the returned containers and tasks refer to different copies and references into the copy stay bound to a hidden manager. `Manager.set_value` promises to update the target and run its dependent tasks, and `copy.deepcopy` of the whole manager keeps the copied graph connected. title: Accelerating RF contour emittance uses symmetric turning points
summary: With an explicit `z`, `RFBucket.emittance_single_particle` computes a contour's longitudinal emittance assuming turning points symmetric about the stable point, although acceleration makes them asymmetric. title: CPU linked-array views bypass dependent-state updates
summary: Writing through a shared CPU slice of `Particles.delta` changes the relative momentum deviation δ without updating the dependent energy and momentum fields, so subsequent tracking uses inconsistent coordinates. title: `Patch(dt)` shifts z but not `Bunch.t_ref`
summary: `Patch(dt)` shifts each particle's longitudinal coordinate z but leaves the bunch reference time `t_ref` unchanged, so the absolute particle time reconstructed from them jumps. A reference-time shift must advance `t_ref` by dt with z and preserve the particle's arrival time t, as the definition z = βc(`t_ref` − t) (β is speed over light speed c) and Bmad's patch implementation require. title: Stored zero dipole strength corrupts coordinates at bend faces
summary: Storing an explicit zero dipole strength in a bend with an enabled nonzero face angle produces NaN coordinates and can mark particles lost. With zero field each particle must follow a straight line to the reference exit plane, as an independent high-precision geometry calculation confirms. Across four geometries with lengths 0.3000–1.100 m and curvatures −0.2500 to 0.4000 m⁻¹, all 24 default-method cases lose all 16 particles instead of transporting them with finite coordinates. Omitting the field entry, setting both face angles to zero, disabling fringes or selecting `Exact()` preserves every particle; in mixed-strength batches exactly the zero-strength lanes fail.

title: Neutron g_spin conflicts with its own-mass normalization contract
summary: The neutron and antineutron `g_spin` values are normalized to the nuclear magneton, which uses the proton mass, although the accessor promises normalization to each particle's own mass. Combining the returned value with the documented formula therefore disagrees with the tabulated magnetic moment, and converting by the neutron-to-proton mass ratio restores agreement. With CODATA 2022 active, neutron `g_spin` with `signed=true` is −3.826 instead of the own-mass value −3.831, implying a gyromagnetic ratio of −1.830 × 10⁸ instead of −1.832 × 10⁸ s⁻¹ T⁻¹, a 0.1377% magnitude error. Antineutron signs reverse with the same fractional error; charged species agree.

title: Coasting `twiss` ignores `delta0`; `a_initial` runs ignore `delta0` and `v0`
summary: For a coasting beam (RF off), `twiss(delta0=δ₀)` finds the closed orbit at the momentum offset δ₀ but tracks the map from δ = 0, and a run started from an initial normalizing map `a_initial` ignores both `delta0` and `v0`. Thin-lens transfer matrices and Jacobians of tracking at δ₀ give the correct optics: for 1 GeV/c electrons in a thin-quadrupole cell at δ₀ = 0.01, `twiss` returns the tune q₁ = 0.1436 and β₁ = 3.441 m instead of 0.1422 and 3.421 m, and `pz` = 0. In a checked ring with dispersion the tabulated orbit does not close and the spin tune is taken at δ = 0. Periodic optics with RF on are unaffected, but `a_initial` still bypasses `v0`.

title: Scalar `d<col>_<n>` returns f⁽ⁿ⁾/n, not the nth derivative
summary: A `twiss` chromatic derivative column `d<col>_<n>` with scalar output, such as `dx_2` or `dbeta1_2`, returns the nth derivative with respect to the momentum offset δ divided by n. title: `h<ijkl>` columns are degree-weighted, and the scalar and Taylor paths disagree
summary: The `twiss` resonance-driving-term columns `h<ijkl>`, the Bengtsson coefficients of the one-turn Lie generator h, are scaled by a monomial-dependent factor, so scalar and Taylor-series outputs disagree. For a thin octupole of integrated strength K3L the documented coefficient is `h2200` = K3L β²/16, and the normal-form tune slope with amplitude independently confirms this normalization. With K3L = 1000 m⁻³ in a thin-quadrupole cell, the octupole's `h2200` increment is 2961 m⁻¹ in scalar output and 1480 m⁻¹ in Taylor output instead of 740.1 m⁻¹, and a thin sextupole gives `h3000` three times its expected value. Scalar coefficients carry the monomial degree as a factor, Taylor coefficients the last contributing exponent, and the chromatic `dh…_n` columns inherit the error.

title: Linear De Moivre `B`/`E` use columns of A⁻¹ instead of rows
summary: In its linear branch (expansion order 1), `twiss` builds the De Moivre matrices `B` and `E`, which split the one-turn matrix and the beam moments by mode, from columns of A⁻¹, the inverse normalizing matrix, instead of its rows. In an uncoupled plane the documented definition gives E₁ = [β −α; −α γ], and the corresponding B₁ matches a tracked one-turn Jacobian to 1.8e-15. For a thin-quadrupole cell with β = 3.441 m and α = −1.376, the returned E₁[1,2] and E₁[2,1] are 0 and 1.776 instead of 1.376, and E₁[2,2] is 0.2906 m⁻¹ instead of 0.8412 m⁻¹. The horizontal beam-size term used by `dynamic_aperture` stays correct in uncoupled lattices; by source algebra, its vertical mode-1 term and coupled lattices are wrong.

title: Summary `alphac` (momentum compaction) equals the slip factor `etac`
summary: The `twiss` summary value `alphac`, labelled the momentum compaction α_p = (1/C) dC/dδ (C the orbit length, δ the relative momentum offset), is computed from the coordinate slip, like the slip factor `etac`. For coasting beams on momentum whose closed orbit has zero longitudinal advance, `alphac` equals `etac` and is low by 1/γ² (γ the Lorentz factor). For 1 GeV/c protons it is −0.4682 instead of 0 in a straight cell and −0.2238 instead of 0.2443 in a cell with bends, as analytic transport and tracking establish. `etac` also loses velocity and closed-orbit time corrections: its straight-cell order-2 δ coefficient is 0.7470 instead of 1.185, and nonzero closed-orbit longitudinal advance corrupts its value. Protons and ions are most affected; ultrarelativistic electron errors are small.

title: Row 2 of the first table column reuses row 1's cache
summary: When the first column of a `twiss` table reads the per-row optics cache, for example with `base_cols=[]` or a custom `base_cols` starting with an optics column, row 2 of that column repeats row 1. Each row must describe its own sample, and drift transport of the start values, β(s) = β₀ − 2α₀s + γ₀s², gives the expected value. title: The spin Lie bracket uses the result field instead of the second input
summary: For vector fields with spin, written as (orbital part, spin quaternion), NonlinearNormalForm's in-place Lie bracket `lb!` uses the result field G instead of the second input H in its spin part, so the bracket is not antisymmetric. The commutator of the package's own Lie operators, and the bracket in Forest's FPP, require the term H·∇f where the code computes G·∇f. For F = (0, x·i) and H = (∂ₓ, 0), the spin component [F,H].q₁ is 0 instead of −1, and for generic polynomial fields the spin part is off by 5.0 in norm while the orbital part is exact. `lb!` is unexported, and its only caller, the correction step of `log`, changes only how fast `log` converges, so no public output is known to change.

title: Spin normal form gives NaN for an exactly vertical (or absent) spin rotation
summary: NonlinearNormalForm's spin normal form throws `InexactError: Float64(NaN + NaN*im)` when the closed-orbit spin axis is exactly vertical or there is no spin rotation. The step that aligns the axis with ŷ divides by a zero axis norm or transverse axis length, although these maps admit a normal form and Forest's FPP handles them explicitly. For a synthetic map that rotates spin by 0.6 rad about ŷ, tilting the axis by 1e-9 rad returns the correct spin-tune magnitude 0.09549 but leaves a transverse quaternion component of 2.96e-10, because the alignment angle loses the tilt. The public `twiss(spin=true)` fails in checked planar rings and straight cells, including RF and coasting cases; the thick-bend quickstart ring escapes only through transverse round-off of order 1e-34.

title: Batched Newton returns the previous iterate's `f` and `jac`
summary: BatchSolve's batched `newton` returns stale `f` and `jac` for lanes (problems in the batch) that the relative-step test accepts in the final iteration: it updates the iterate, then exits before recomputing the promised final residual and Jacobian. For x² − 2 from x = 1 with `reltol = 0.4`, the accepted iterate is 1.5, but the returned residual and Jacobian are −1.000 and 2.000 instead of 0.2500 and 3.000; the non-batched solver returns the latter values. By source inspection, batched closed-orbit finding uses this path and experimental aperture code reads the Jacobian as I − M, with M the one-turn matrix.

title: Allocating `newton`/`brent` document caller mutation they do not do
summary: The docstrings of BatchSolve's allocating `newton` and `brent` say that the returned solution `u` is the caller's `x`, mutated in place, but both work on a copy and leave `x` unchanged. The in-place `brent!` does alias its argument, so the text describes the in-place functions. Calling `newton` from x = [2.0] returns u = [1.000] and leaves x = [2.0], with `u === x` false. Code that follows the docstring and reads `x` after the call gets the initial guess. The allocating behavior itself is sensible; only the documentation is wrong.

title: NAFF's Gram–Schmidt step is conjugated and unnormalized
summary: FundamentalFrequencies' `naff` (Numerical Analysis of Fundamental Frequencies) uses a conjugated, unnormalized Gram–Schmidt projection, corrupting later spectral lines and amplitudes. Under the package's own inner product, removing an earlier basis signal Uⱼ from Uᵢ requires the coefficient ⟨Uᵢ,Uⱼ⟩/⟨Uⱼ,Uⱼ⟩, and a corrected projection restores orthogonality. For 513 samples over 512 intervals with frequencies 0.2134, 0.2179 and 0.3171 cycles per sample and amplitudes 1, 0.6 and 0.02, the third reported line rediscovers the first and has zero amplitude. Correcting the projection and amplitude normalization recovers the missing 0.3171 line with amplitude 0.02000. The first two frequency estimates are unchanged by that correction, and changing `tol` has no effect.

title: Orbital caps of 1 drop the start-point dispersion feed-down (default `twiss(chrom=2)`, documented knob descriptors)
summary: With `twiss(chrom=2)`, the default GTPSA descriptor caps each phase-space coordinate at degree 1 and so drops the squares x² and pₓ² that carry the dispersion feed-down, silently corrupting chromatic optics. Chromaticity is dQ/dδ of the one-turn map linearized on the momentum-dependent closed orbit; tracking and `twiss(order=2, chrom=2)` agree on it. In the documentation's 18 GeV/c electron FODO with sextupoles, started where the dispersion is 0.5317 m, ξₓ is +0.1220 instead of −0.06914 and `dbeta1` is −39.28 m instead of −30.65 m, and the documented matching recipe reaches a tracked ξₓ of 0.5128 instead of 1. Dispersive starts with feed-down from bends or multipoles, and the documented low-cap knob descriptors for orbit-moving knobs without dispersion, show the error; on-momentum linear optics stay correct.

title: Summary tunes and `phi` columns alias when a sampled segment exceeds half a turn
summary: `twiss` builds the summary tunes and the `phi` phase-advance columns by adding the principal phase angle, in (−½, ½] turn, of each interval between sampled rows, so an interval longer than half a turn aliases the integer part. For a ring of eight thin FODO cells, sampling only element 17 (`at=[17]`, after four cells) gives q₁ = −0.8515 instead of 1.149 and a phase of −0.4257 instead of 0.5743 turns at s = 8 m; thin-lens matrix products and sampling every cell establish the accumulated values. The documented summary-only `at=[]` call treats the ring as one interval and returns 0.1485. Fractional tunes stay correct; the integer part is lost wherever an interval between sampled rows exceeds half a turn.

title: Reading a monomial the descriptor does not hold terminates the process
summary: In GTPSA, reading the coefficient of a monomial that the descriptor does not hold ends the Julia process from the C library with the message `invalid monomial`, with no Julia exception or stack trace; code in `catch`, `finally` and `atexit` never runs. An out-of-range indexing call should throw a catchable exception, and GTPSA's own validity test `mad_desc_isvalidm` already identifies such monomials. For t = (x + y)² under `Descriptor([1,1,1], 2)`, whose per-variable caps of 1 exclude every square, `t[[1,1,0]]` correctly returns 2.000, but `t[[2,0,0]]` ends the session with exit status 1. Per-variable caps, such as those of the default `twiss(chrom=2)` descriptor, make such reads easy to issue; by source reading, the monomial setter lacks the same check.

summary: `getterm` returns 0.0 for coefficients of the summary tunes, `etac` and `alphac` that the descriptor admits but the normal form never computes, because its guard checks only the requested monomial. title: `copy!` into a `VectorField` drops the spin part, so `log` never corrects its spin generator
summary: NonlinearNormalForm's `copy!` omits a `VectorField` destination's quaternion, its spin part, so copies and typed conversions lose spin and `log` never receives its spin correction. For a constant rotation generated by (0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.05), `log` returns its unchanged initial guess (−0.02614, 0.09913, 0.1983, 0.04956), so the defining round trip exp(log M) = M fails; copying the quaternion restores the analytic generator to round-off. title: `twiss` with `h` columns and `spin=true` ends the process (division by a zero quaternion)
summary: On rings where spin optics succeeds, requesting `h<ijkl>` columns (resonance driving terms) with `spin=true` ends the Julia process while `twiss` builds the Hamiltonian. The temporary linear map built there has a zero quaternion, and inverting it divides by zero in the native library, which bypasses Julia exception handling. For the 18 GeV electron quickstart FODO at order 2, the call prints `invalid domain div` and exits with status 1. Giving that map the identity quaternion lets the checked orbital coefficients agree with `spin=false` to 1.990e-14, as the decoupling of orbital and spin motion requires. title: `TPSAMap` composition transports covariance at the wrong expansion point
summary: When NonlinearNormalForm composes stochastic `TPSAMap`s, which carry a noise covariance S, it transports the incoming covariance with the second map's Jacobian at that map's own expansion point instead of at the incoming orbit. title: Montague functions omit momentum normalization
summary: In uncoupled transverse optics, the scalar Montague chromatic functions `w`, W = √(A² + B²) built from the δ-derivatives β′ and α′ of the Twiss functions, use canonical-coordinate beta derivatives without the standard momentum normalization. With δ the relative momentum offset, the angle-coordinate beta is β_angle = (1+δ)β_c, so B requires β_c′/β_c + 1/(1+δ), and A = α_c′ − α_cB. Analytic drift transport and exact rational propagation confirm that momentum-independent angle ellipses have W = 0. For entrance (β_angle, α) = (2 m, 0.3) and (3 m, −0.2), `twiss` instead gives W = 1.044 and 1.020 initially, then 1.080 and 1.193 after 1.3 m of drift. This corrupts the chromatic-amplitude diagnostic without invalidating the canonical-coordinate beta convention itself.

title: Sextupole spin fringes use twice the longitudinal field
summary: Normal and skew sextupole fringes apply twice the leading longitudinal-field spin rotation at both the entrance and the exit. title: Sagan RF spin impulses omit the superimposed solenoid vector potential
summary: A `SaganCavity` with a superimposed solenoid field and zero active RF length (`L_active=0`) uses canonical transverse momenta directly in its RF spin kick instead of first subtracting the solenoid vector potential. By the Thomas–BMT equation, a longitudinal electric field gives no spin rotation for longitudinal mechanical motion, and independent high-precision solenoid transport preserves an initially longitudinal spin. For off-axis protons initially moving and polarized longitudinally, with P₀c (reference momentum times light speed) twice the rest energy, a 0.4300 m element of normalized solenoid strength 1.400 m⁻¹ and RF energy gain 1.877 keV produces a maximum transverse spin of 2.727 × 10⁻⁷ instead of zero. title: IBS uses canonical momenta for flight time inside a solenoid
summary: Inside a solenoid, the intrabeam scattering (IBS) kick computes flight time and particle survival from canonical transverse momenta without subtracting the solenoid vector potential. A translation of the bunch that preserves mechanical momenta must preserve every collision kick, as independent Lorentz-helix tracking and the unchanged bunch covariance confirm. For 64 protons with reference momentum 3mc (m the proton mass, c the speed of light), normalized solenoid strength 8.000 m⁻¹ and slice length 7.813 mm, a 31.25 mm horizontal translation changes the largest impulse by 0.8438% of the unshifted value instead of zero. title: IBS momentum impulses omit the speed-dependent longitudinal conversion
summary: Deterministic intrabeam-scattering (IBS) impulses change particle speed without rescaling the longitudinal coordinate z, shifting the represented arrival time. The coordinate definition z = βc(t_ref − t), where β is speed divided by the speed of light c, t_ref is reference time and t is arrival time, requires z_out = z_in β_out/β_in at a fixed event. For a 1.230 nC electron bunch at reference kinetic energy 60.32 keV, an impulse assigned to a 7.000 cm drift produces a maximum time jump of 1.115 fs instead of zero. An isolated impulse and independent Cartesian flight calculation agree; disabling IBS preserves time to 9.530 × 10⁻²⁶ s.

title: Rigidity sign "correction" keeps a negative rigidity for positive species
summary: Giving a positive species a negative reference rigidity `p_over_q_ref`, in the `Beamline` constructor, by assignment or by switching `species_ref` from electron to proton, logs a sign correction but keeps the negative value. Signed rigidity R obeys pc = qRc with a forward reference momentum, so R must carry the sign of the charge q; the same state requested through `pc_ref` is rejected. For a proton line given `p_over_q_ref` = −3, the stored reference is R = −3.000 T·m, `pc_ref` = −0.8994 GeV and `E_ref` = −1.300 GeV, instead of +3.000 T·m, +0.8994 GeV and +1.300 GeV. Negatively charged species are corrected; for positive species every absolute reference quantity derived from the rigidity has the wrong sign.

title: Harmonic RF frequency uses branch-global `s`, not the containing Beamline length
summary: A harmonic-number cavity's `rf_frequency` getter and its tracking setup take as circumference the branch-global end position `s` of the cavity's Beamline, which includes every upstream Beamline of the `Branch`. The documentation defines `harmon` relative to the containing Beamline's own length, and the same cavity Beamline standing alone gives exactly that frequency. title: Bmad SciBmad writer's Context `c1` overwrites a Bmad element named `c1`
summary: Bmad's SciBmad exporter binds the lattice's variable Context to the name `c1` after defining elements, overwriting any element whose name becomes `c1`. Bmad names are case-insensitive, so both `c1` and `C1` trigger the collision. Loading then fails with “Unable to construct Branch: entry 2 of elements is a Context{Any}”, while the same lattice with element name `c2` loads. A Branch named `c1` instead overwrites the Context and also prevents loading; renaming only the generated Context binding and its final reference makes the tested collisions load. The exporter gives no incomplete-translation warning.

title: `BatchParam` scalar shortcuts test `≈ 0` and `≈ 1`, dropping factors, derivatives and knobs
summary: Arithmetic between a scalar and an array-backed `BatchParam` (addition, subtraction, multiplication and batch/scalar division) takes shortcuts when the scalar is approximately 0 or 1, discarding derivatives and power-series terms. ForwardDiff multipliers at 1 lose their derivatives, zero cases depend on the signs of the zero and the derivative, and GTPSA series with scalar part 0 or 1 lose their nonconstant coefficients. For a 0.5 m quadrupole with `Kn1 = s * BatchParam([0.3, 0.6])` and initial x = 1 mm, dx/ds at s = 1 is [0, 0] instead of [−1.833×10⁻⁴, −3.583×10⁻⁴] m, which scalar tracking and finite differences recover. Float64 factors within a relative 1.490×10⁻⁸ of 1 and Float32 factors within 3.453×10⁻⁴ are ignored, and division by zero gives +∞ in every lane.

title: A ForwardDiff or GTPSA scalar combined with a Float32 `BatchParam` throws
summary: Combining a ForwardDiff `Dual` or a GTPSA power-series scalar with a Float32 array-backed `BatchParam` fails when the operation reaches scalar conversion: `Dual(2.0, 1.0) * BatchParam(Float32[1, -2])` raises a `Float32(::Dual)` method error, and a power series with constant part 2 fails conversion to Float32 the same way. The conversion, meant to preserve lane precision, is wrongly applied to these richer scalar types. The same `Dual` with a Float64 batch gives values [2, −4] and derivatives [1, −2], the lane-wise result. Single-precision batch differentiation through this path fails before tracking on the CPU; the approximate-zero/one shortcuts instead bypass the conversion and silently lose derivative terms.

title: Simultaneous magnetic-strength convention changes rescale the partner twice
summary: A magnetic strength can be set as a field (B) or normalized to rigidity (K), integrated or per unit length. Reassigning a nonzero strength its current value through a name that changes both choices at once rescales the unassigned normal or skew partner by an extra L or 1/L, where L is the element length; this self-assignment must preserve the field, as two successive single-change self-assignments do. For a proton dipole with L = 0.25 m, rigidity R = 7.3 T·m, `Bn0` = −0.21 T and `Bs0` = 0.13 T, assigning `Kn0L` its own value keeps the kick Δpx = 7.192×10⁻³ but reduces Δpy from 4.452×10⁻³, the uniform-field Lorentz-force value, to 1.113×10⁻³. A zero partner or L = 1 m hides the error.

title: Finite EHKICK bends sloped particles on the wrong radius and leaves yp unchanged
summary: A finite-length EHKICK with a nonzero kick mistracks particles with nonzero vertical slope y′: it uses total momentum to set the projected bend radius and changes horizontal slope x′ while keeping y′ fixed. A uniform vertical field conserves total and vertical momentum, requiring a helix whose radius depends on momentum perpendicular to the field, as independent Lorentz-force integrations confirm. For a 0.7 m magnet with a 0.09 rad kick, a particle 20% above reference momentum entering with x′ = 0.08 and y′ = 0.06 leaves with y′ = 0.06000 instead of 0.06054, losing 0.8842% of its vertical momentum. At 1 mrad kick and slopes, y′ is 1.500 nrad too small; particles without vertical slope are unaffected.

title: KQUAD fringes use the stored gradient instead of the effective body gradient
summary: When KQUAD is specified by pole-tip field B and bore radius BORE, or has fractional strength error FSE, its body resolves the effective gradient but both fringes use the stored K₁. With B/BORE and default K₁ = 0, a matrix or Twiss request changes tracking by populating that stored value; FSE is still omitted. For a 0.4 m magnet at electron momentum 2000 mₑc, the field-input error reaches 1.749 µrad, while K₁ = 5 m⁻² with FSE = 0.2 differs from the equivalent K₁ = 6 m⁻² magnet by 419.4 nrad. Equivalent-field and zero-field controls establish that both fringes must use the same effective gradient as the body.

title: Zero-voltage MODRF and RAMPRF advance the arrival time by L instead of the slanted path length
summary: With VOLT = 0, MODRF and RAMPRF move particles along straight lines but advance the longitudinal coordinate by cavity length L, omitting the extra path L(√(1 + x′² + y′²) − 1) for transverse slopes x′ and y′. A nonzero nominal voltage with exactly zero effective field gives the full slanted-path time, as an exact-drift control confirms. For L = 1.7 m and electron momentum 2 mₑc with x′ = 0.03 and y′ = −0.02, arrival is at 6.340 ns instead of 6.344 ns, 4.120 ps early.

summary: RFDF computes particle speed at entrance and reuses it for drift timing after kicks change the momentum. title: MODRF damped phase modulation keeps an undamped local frequency
summary: With damped phase modulation, MODRF uses a local angular frequency that is not the derivative of its bunch-centroid phase. The frequency omits both exponential attenuation and the derivative of the damping envelope, so the energy variation within the bunch disagrees with the specified phase waveform. For a 200 MHz, 10 kV cavity with 25° phase modulation at 90 MHz, decay rate α = 4 × 10⁸ s⁻¹ and bunch-centre time T = 2 ns, the slope dγ/dt is −2.383 × 10⁷ s⁻¹ instead of −2.255 × 10⁷ s⁻¹, 5.711% too steep; γ is the Lorentz factor. The manual specifies the same local-frequency formula.

title: Finite matrix RFCA assigns the whole transit to the entrance speed
summary: An RFCA of nonzero length using the default matrix method (N_KICKS = 0) times the entire cavity at the entrance speed despite modeling acceleration in its transverse response. For a 0.75 m, 160 kV cavity at crest and electron momentum p = 2.3 mₑc, the 2.728 ns transit exceeds the allowed upper limit by 27.45 ps. The minimum timing errors fall to 0.3778 ps at 10 mₑc and 0.3902 fs at 100 mₑc.

title: CSBEND edge model 3 is documented as symplectic but its finite-gap kick is not six-dimensionally symplectic
summary: The manual recommends CSBEND edge model 3 for applications requiring symplecticity, without restricting the claim to transverse motion at fixed energy. With a finite pole gap, its momentum-dependent vertical kick omits the time shift needed for a six-dimensional canonical map. In a 0.9 m, 0.23 rad bend, a particle with relative momentum offset δ = 0.15 and vertical offset y = 20 mm receives no exit-edge path shift, while canonical completion requires Δs = −2.222×10⁻⁷ m. The measured six-dimensional symplecticity residual is 2.224×10⁻⁵, despite a transverse residual below 3.5×10⁻¹³. The completion is not a measured physical fringe delay.

title: CSBEND spin tracking passes canonical momenta to the slope-based spin update
summary: With spin tracking enabled, CSBEND's unexpanded-Hamiltonian integrator passes canonical momenta to a spin routine that expects slopes, giving incorrect electron spin precession. For initial spin (0, 0, 1) in a planar 1.2 m, 0.22 rad bend at reference momentum p₀ = 800 mₑc, relative momentum offset δ = 0.4 and entrance slope x′ = 0.16, exact circular motion and Thomas–BMT predict an exit spin angle of −0.1552 rad relative to the exit reference axis. Tracking converges to −0.1605 rad, an error of 5.297 mrad that slice refinement cannot remove. The on-axis, on-momentum control agrees.

title: POLAR random-direction modes give NaN spins along a longitudinal axis
summary: With spin tracking enabled, POLAR's narrow-cone, wide-cone and von Mises–Fisher modes return NaN (not-a-number) spin components for every tested particle when the polarization axis is (0, 0, ±1). At requested polarizations P = 0.25 and 0.8, all 12 spins become nonfinite without warning; the tilted axis (0.6, 0, 0.8) gives 12 finite unit spins. Rotations should preserve unit spin length, and a narrow cone should satisfy S·v = P, where S is the spin and v the unit axis. The rotation these modes share is singular on that axis, so by source inspection the failure extends to every 0 < P < 1.

title: GKICKMAP applies classical radiation loss with SYNCH_RAD disabled
summary: Selecting ISR = 1 with SYNCH_RAD = 0 in GKICKMAP also applies classical radiation loss, despite the switches independently selecting excitation and mean loss. In a one-slice, 0.6 m map at reference momentum p₀ = 4200 mₑc, with entrance slope x′ = 0.004 and horizontal slope kick 0.025, the unwanted relative-momentum loss is 1.450×10⁻⁷. A separate small-angle radiation calculation agrees with the classical-only control within 10⁻¹⁶, while the radiation-free control preserves momentum. title: UKICKMAP loss compaction gives survivors extra radiation updates
summary: With classical radiation enabled in UKICKMAP, removing an out-of-map particle can apply one extra radiation update to the survivor moved into its place. The same identified survivors therefore lose different momentum when unrelated lost particles are listed before them rather than after them, although nominal loss must be independent of row order. For electrons at reference momentum p₀ = 5100 mₑc in a 0.16 m map with undulator parameter K = 2.4, one period gives relative momentum offset δ = −1.362×10⁻⁸ instead of −6.808×10⁻⁹; two periods give −4.085×10⁻⁸ instead of −2.723×10⁻⁸. Independent radiation-integral recurrences and no-loss and loss-last controls establish the extra update.

title: Yawed kick maps sample half a slice behind the particle
summary: In GKICKMAP and UKICKMAP, yaw alignment evaluates the map-axis displacement at the slice entrance after the particle has drifted to the slice midpoint. The resulting horizontal sampling error is h tan ψ/2, where h is the slice length and ψ the yaw angle, so a particle following the map's zero-force axis receives a false kick. For a 0.7 m device with ψ = 0.013 rad and slope kick Δx′ = −(0.08 m⁻¹)x at local horizontal offset x, three slices give slope error −1.203×10⁻⁴ instead of zero; 12 slices give −3.005×10⁻⁵.

title: LSRMDLTR radiation loss scales with the cube of the reference momentum
summary: With classical radiation enabled in the LSRMDLTR laser modulator, an electron's calculated momentum loss changes when only the reference momentum changes. For particle momentum p and reference momentum p₀ in units of mₑc, the implemented local loss rate is (p₀/γ)³ times the classical rate, where γ = √(1 + p²) is the Lorentz factor. title: TMCF fiducial timing uses transverse positions as momentum components
summary: A TMCF cavity using a particle fiducial, including the serial default t,median, estimates transit time using transverse positions instead of slopes. title: MAPSOLENOID combined misalignment rotations are not mutual inverses
summary: In Elegant's MAPSOLENOID, the misalignment angles ETILT, EYAW and EPITCH rotate the particle into the element frame with one matrix and rotate the field back with another that is not its inverse when more than one angle is nonzero. With a 0.7 m map of 1.200 mT, p = 13 mₑc, ETILT = 0.17, EYAW = −0.11 and EPITCH = 0.13 rad, the slopes change by −8.214×10⁻⁴ (x′) and −8.546×10⁻⁴ (y′) instead of zero; each angle alone is exact. title: RFCA subtracts its CHANGE_T clock-wrap interval once per kick
summary: In an RFCA with CHANGE_T = 1, a nonzero interval T of whole RF periods is subtracted at each of N integration kicks but added to the clock only once. Laboratory arrival time, stored time plus clock, shifts by −(N−1)T although the energy is unchanged, so downstream time-dependent elements act at the wrong time. For a 0.135 m, 24 kV, 0.8 GHz cavity with N = 3 and electron momentum p = 7 mₑc, T = 6.250 ns and the shift is −12.50 ns. A downstream BUMPER gives horizontal slope x′ = 1.475×10⁻³ instead of 1.388×10⁻³, as checked by an independent laboratory-time recurrence. One effective kick is unaffected.

summary: KQUAD and KSEXT magnets sharing a STEERING_MULTIPOLES filename share mutable coefficients scaled by each magnet's STEERING_MULTIPOLE_FACTOR. title: Negative CCBEND edge multipole signs are chosen from the body table's order labels
summary: Negative-angle CCBEND magnets with independent entrance or exit multipole-error files choose edge sign changes from the body table's order labels. Relabelling zero-amplitude body rows therefore changes physical edge kicks; shorter body tables can also corrupt kicks, and runs without body tables terminate. With zero body-error amplitudes, the reference is a positive bend rotated by π with each order-n edge fraction multiplied by (−1)ⁿ. title: SOLE spin transport misses the precession along off-axis trajectories and the edge-field rotations
summary: With spin tracking enabled, a SOLE solenoid rotates each spin once about its longitudinal field at the exit slopes, so off-axis or sloped particles miss both the precession along their rotating trajectory in the body and the spin rotations by the radial edge fields that the orbital matrix includes. title: CCBEND with ETILT as its only error skips the entrance misalignment transform
summary: A CCBEND whose only error is the roll ETILT, with DX, DY, DZ, EPITCH and EYAW all zero, applies the misalignment transform at the exit but not at the entrance. summary: A CSBEND with EXPAND_HAMILTONIAN=1 and ISR=1 gives every radiation kick the step length s/3, although integration orders 2, 4 and 6 have 1, 3 and 7 kicks per step of length s. title: Identical CCBENDs that share a tracking-based matrix lose the path-length reference correction

title: RFCA with Q ramps its voltage as the square root of a stored-energy fill, not as a resonant fill

title: Third-order concatenation multiplies spurious path-origin terms of tracking-derived maps by the accumulated path length
summary: Elegant derives CCBEND maps by tracking, and those maps carry spurious terms that depend on the incoming path coordinate s. title: Tracking tune shift with amplitude ignores nuy_roi_width and the amplitude scaling factors
summary: In tracking mode, Elegant's `tune_shift_with_amplitude` searches the vertical tune peak within `nux_roi_width` and never reads `nuy_roi_width`, `scale_down_factor`, `scale_up_factor` or `scale_up_limit`, all documented in the manual. title: Tracking tune shift with amplitude retries without end when NAFF finds no tune in its window
summary: In tracking mode, Elegant's `tune_shift_with_amplitude` treats a failed NAFF tune analysis as a lost particle, shrinks the amplitudes and retries, resetting its retry counter each time, so an analysis that fails at every amplitude never ends the run. title: rf_setup sets the electron's synchronous phase for positrons and protons
summary: After `change_particle` selects a positron or a proton, `rf_setup` gives the RFCA and MODRF cavities the electron's synchronous phase, although these cavities reverse the energy gain of positively charged particles. The positron's cavity then removes the radiation loss per turn U₀ instead of replacing it, and the synchrotron motion of either species grows exponentially. By charge conjugation the correct phase is the electron's plus 180°, which `phase_offset=180` applies. In a 98 m ring at 2.044 GeV with U₀ = 202.1 keV and 1 MV, positrons get 168.3° instead of 348.3°, lose 404.2 keV in the first turn, and the one-turn longitudinal map trace is 2.094 (amplitude growth 1.357 per turn) instead of the stable 1.906.

title: Resonance driving terms omit fractional strength errors applied by tracking
summary: With `compute_driving_terms` enabled, `twiss_output` uses nominal multipole strengths even when tracking applies fractional strength errors. title: Manual orders tune_shift_with_amplitude after twiss_output, where Elegant rejects or ignores it
summary: The Elegant manual says `tune_shift_with_amplitude` must follow `twiss_output`. Given in that order with Twiss output scheduled for each step (`output_at_each_step=1`), Elegant stops with "you must give tune_shift_with_amplitude before twiss_output"; after an immediate `twiss_output`, Elegant has already written the Twiss file, so no tune shift is computed and dnux/dAx and the other tune-shift columns stay 0. For eight FODO cells with a thin octupole of integrated strength K₃L, that order gives dnux/dAx = 1.411 m⁻¹, within 0.02% of the first-order detuning K₃L βx²/(32π), while the documented order gives an error or 0.

title: Pelegant falsely warns that fast-orbit-feedback BPM readings are not reduced across ranks
summary: When a user runs the fast orbit feedback command under MPI (Pelegant), Elegant warns that beam-position-monitor (BPM) readings are not reduced across ranks, which would leave each rank's monitor reading only its own particles. The warning is therefore false for these readings, although the manual says Pelegant results are identical to serial for a deterministic beam.

title: Round nonlinear space charge omits the integrating length and optics weighting
summary: With `insert_sceffects` and `nonlinear=1`, SCMULT omits the integrating length and optical weights from the kick of a round Gaussian beam. The branch is selected when the rms sizes σₓ and σᵧ satisfy |σₓ − σᵧ|/σₓ < 10⁻⁶; an unsliced Gaussian control with σᵧ/σₓ = 1 + 10⁻⁵ agrees with an independent integrated-field calculation. In a symmetric ring with 1 nC of electrons at 10 mₑc and σₓ = σᵧ = 1 mm, the round kick is 4.000 times the correct value after a 0.25 m drift and 1.333 times it after a 0.75 m drift.

title: Single-precision reciprocals in the complex error function reduce the Gaussian force accuracy

title: WAKE cache substitutes the first requested column pair
summary: When two WAKE elements in one Elegant run select different wake columns (WCOLUMN) or time columns (TCOLUMN) from the same table file, the second element silently reuses the first element's columns, because the table is cached by file name alone. For a table with kernels A and B = 3A, the earliest particles of a 12-electron, 2 nC bunch should lose the sum of both kernels, 8000 eV; the shared file gives 4000 eV (A applied twice) or 12000 eV (B applied twice), depending on element order, which is an error of −50% or +50%. A byte-identical copy of the table under another file name gives the correct result.

title: BEAMBEAM kicks change arrival time because s is not rescaled
summary: A BEAMBEAM kick changes momentum but leaves the stored longitudinal coordinate s = βct unchanged, where t is arrival time, c is the speed of light and β is speed divided by c. title: Dipole resonators create momentum in the disabled plane
summary: When TRFMODE or FTRFMODE tracks a dipole mode in one plane only, its longitudinal kick creates momentum in the other plane in proportion to the incoming slope there. title: Later SCMULT bunches use the exit beta function for the entrance weight
summary: When Elegant tracks a bunch train with SCMULT space-charge kicks (`insert_sceffects` in bunch mode), every bunch after the first integrates the space-charge strength over each element with the element's exit beta function β in place of its entrance value, so identical bunches receive different kicks. title: TRWAKE quadrupole probe coordinates omit element misalignment
summary: TRWAKE quadrupole wakes (probe exponents 1, drive exponents 0) use each particle's global transverse coordinate even when the structure has misalignments DX and DY. title: SCMULT keeps stale beam sizes across zero-length elements that change them
summary: SCMULT measures the beam sizes for its space-charge strength only at exits of elements with positive length, so after a zero-length element that changes the transverse sizes, such as an EMATRIX or ROTATE, the next segment pairs the old sizes with the new beta functions. title: insert_sceffects clear leaves a negative specification count, crashing or silently dropping every SCMULT
summary: Setting clear = 1 on insert_sceffects decrements the count of insertion specifications to −1 instead of 0, so the next specification is written one entry before its array. Clearing and replacing an earlier command with the same selector then completes with no SCMULT and no warning, so the run has no space charge; clearing in a fresh run, clearing alone, and clearing with disable = 1 after an earlier command crash. The manual says clear deletes prior insertions and disable makes a command ignored, so each run must complete, and all but the lone clear must insert one SCMULT. In a one-segment ring with a 0.8000 nC bunch, the replacement's expected linear slope kick of 2.379×10⁻⁴ becomes exactly zero.

title: CSRCSBEND computes CSR with the nominal bend radius, ignoring the field error FSE
summary: CSRCSBEND computes the CSR strength, the transient slippage length and the argument of the integrated Green function (IGF=1) from the nominal radius ρ = L/ANGLE, although FSE, the documented field-strength error, bends the orbit on the radius ρ/(1 + FSE). title: CSRCSBEND with IGF=1 and BIN_SIZE writes past its Green-function arrays when the bunch lengthens
summary: With IGF=1 and BIN_SIZE, CSRCSBEND sizes its integrated-Green-function arrays for the bin count of its first slice and fills them up to the current bin count in every later slice. title: Longitudinal space charge uses an unpadded FFT, so an isolated bunch gets the field of a train spaced by its own length
summary: LSCDRIFT, and the longitudinal space charge of RFCW and CSRDRIFT, apply the impedance with a discrete Fourier transform over a window three bins longer than the bunch's sampled extent, without zero padding, so the field is that of a periodic train of bunch copies. title: WAKE gives each particle the full W(0) of its own bin, so full-origin wakes such as CORGPIPE's overstate the loss
summary: With default binning and gather settings, WAKE uses the full table value W(0) for charge in a particle’s own bin. WAKE’s manual leaves the origin convention unspecified; tables already containing W(0⁺)/2 avoid this endpoint excess.

title: LRWAKE keeps more turns of wake history than TURNS_TO_KEEP after an end bunch is lost
summary: When an end bunch of a multibunch beam is lost, LRWAKE keeps more turns of wake sources than TURNS_TO_KEEP requests. Its history holds TURNS_TO_KEEP times the initial bunch count but advances on each pass by only the surviving count, so stale turns are never dropped; the correct loss sums the sources of the requested turns, as tracking without a loss confirms. For two 1.000 nC bunches at 511.0 MeV/c in a constant 1.000×10¹² V/C longitudinal wake with TURNS_TO_KEEP = 2, the surviving bunch loses 3.000 keV per pass instead of 1.000 keV from the third pass on, whichever end bunch was lost. title: WAKE and TRWAKE manuals say ACAUSAL_ALLOWED=0 enables acausal wakes; Elegant requires 1
summary: The WAKE and TRWAKE manual pages state that acausal wakes, tabulated from negative times, are supported provided the user sets ACAUSAL_ALLOWED=0. Elegant does the opposite: with ACAUSAL_ALLOWED=0, the default, a table that does not start at t = 0 stops the run with an error asking for ACAUSAL_ALLOWED=1, as the parameter descriptions and the release note that introduced the feature say. With ACAUSAL_ALLOWED=1 both elements apply the acausal wake as tabulated: for two electron groups 3 ps apart and a wake that is nonzero only at negative times, the leading group loses 12.00 keV in WAKE and receives a 3.914×10⁻⁷ rad kick in TRWAKE, equal to the direct pair sums.

title: WAKE manual says ALLOW_LONG_BEAM ignores the beam's far part, but Elegant keeps the whole beam
summary: The WAKE manual says that when the beam is longer than the wake data and ALLOW_LONG_BEAM is nonzero, Elegant warns and ignores the part of the beam furthest from the mean arrival time in computing the wake. Elegant warns but bins and kicks the whole beam; the trimming is commented out in the source. For a 0.8 nC beam of 90 electrons at t = 0 and satellite groups of 10 at 50 ps and 51 ps, with 20 ps of wake data, the manual's algorithm keeps only the main group and gives no loss, whereas the 51 ps group loses 2182 eV, the whole-beam pair sum.

title: MPI Touschek generation crashes when tracking is disabled
summary: When Pelegant, Elegant's MPI version, runs the touschek_scatter command with its default do_track = 0, which generates the scattered particles without tracking them, it crashes with a segmentation fault after generating the particles at the first TSCATTER element. title: MATTER collision slices omit incoming transverse drift
summary: When MATTER uses single scattering in a finite-length target, each slice containing a collision omits the transverse drift from the slope entering that slice. Correct transport must include that slope times the slice length, in addition to the displacement from the scattering kick. In a one-slice, 0.01 m helium target, shifting the incoming horizontal and vertical slopes by 0.002 and −0.003 leaves all scattered electrons' exit positions unchanged, instead of shifting them by 20.00 µm and −30.00 µm; unscattered electrons drift correctly. Earlier kicks can also expose the error in later slices.

title: Standalone electron recoil omits energy loss
summary: In MATTER, enabling ELECTRON_RECOIL while ENERGY_DECAY and NUCLEAR_BREMSSTRAHLUNG are disabled omits the documented recoil energy loss. The energy-processing gates ignore standalone recoil, although collisions with target electrons must transfer positive energy. For 20000 electrons of momentum 1000 mₑc crossing 0.01 m of dilute helium, a Poisson approximation to the option's event rate predicts 6894 ± 67.21 electrons losing energy, but recoil-only output is bit-identical to all-off output. Enabling bremsstrahlung activates thousands of recoil losses, isolating the activation failure.

title: Active recoil transfers use inconsistent energy normalization
summary: For relativistic electrons in MATTER with ELECTRON_RECOIL and NUCLEAR_BREMSSTRAHLUNG enabled, recoil-transfer rates are suppressed by about the momentum P, measured in mₑc, at transfers above binding energies and small compared with incident kinetic energy. The event rate contains 1/P, but sampled transfers are subtracted directly from the Lorentz factor γ. For 20000 electrons at P = 1000 crossing 0.01 m of dilute helium, the free-electron Møller integral predicts 42.22 electrons losing at least 1.022 keV; serial and three-rank parallel runs give none despite active recoil sampling. The Poisson probability of zero such transfers under that reference is 4.408×10⁻¹⁹.

summary: With the smooth method (SMOOTH=1), an IBSCATTER element applies the intrabeam-scattering growth to all three planes whatever the plane switches DO_X, DO_Y and DO_Z say. title: Smooth IBS shifts the beam centroid when there is dispersion and a momentum offset
summary: With the smooth method (SMOOTH=1), IBSCATTER measures the beam centroid c and scales the transverse coordinates about c + ημ, where η is the dispersion and μ the beam's mean fractional momentum offset δ. The centroid already contains the dispersive displacement ημ, so the origin is displaced twice and the centroid moves by (1−a)ημ, where a is the amplitude growth factor, instead of staying fixed. In a closed ring with η = 14.29 m and μ = 1×10⁻⁴, an amplitude growth of 0.8501% moves the mean horizontal position by −12.14 µm instead of 0; with μ = 0 it stays put.

title: CBSCAT computes a negative Klein–Nishina total cross section just above its Thomson cutoff
summary: When Elegant's CBSCAT element, which models laser Compton scattering, uses its default Klein–Nishina cross section, the total cross section it evaluates just above ε = 10⁻⁶ can be negative, where ε is the laser photon energy in the electron rest frame divided by mₑc². Cancellation between large terms destroys the result, and then no electron scatters. For 25 mₑc electrons, a head-on laser and a Thomson probability of 0.025, the code's total is −28.95 times the Thomson value at ε = 1.200×10⁻⁶ instead of 1.000, and none of 24000 electrons scatters instead of about 600; at ε = 5.000×10⁻⁶ the ratio is 0.6069 and 345 scatter.

title: Approximate CBSCAT recoil depends on the reference momentum
summary: With the approximate recoil of Elegant's CBSCAT element (CROSS_SECTION="thomson", EXACT_RECOIL=0), the momentum an electron loses in a laser Compton scatter depends on the reference momentum P₀ the user chose, although the physics does not. The code computes the fractional change ΔP/P of the electron's momentum P and adds it to δ = P/P₀ − 1, which requires ΔP/P₀. For 12 mₑc electrons and a 30 µm laser, the same 454 scattered electrons lose a mean 2.303×10⁻⁵ mₑc at P₀ = 12 mₑc, 1.152×10⁻⁵ mₑc at P₀ = 6 mₑc and 4.607×10⁻⁵ mₑc at P₀ = 24 mₑc.

title: Thin forced-MCS MATTER omits the flight distance from the transverse angles
summary: With FORCE_MCS=1 in a MATTER element thinner than 0.001 radiation lengths and ENERGY_DECAY=0, Elegant advances the longitudinal coordinate by the axial length L alone. At speed βc, the flight time must be at least √(L² + Δx² + Δy²)/(βc), where Δx and Δy are transverse displacements between the endpoints. In dilute helium with L = 0.4 m, electrons at momentum 2.000 mₑc with slopes (0.001, 0.003) violate this bound by 7.459×10⁻¹⁵ s; at 2.400 mₑc with slopes (−0.02, 0.015), the deficit is 4.516×10⁻¹³ s.

title: MATTER recoil probability per slice exceeds one and saturates
summary: In MATTER with ELECTRON_RECOIL and NUCLEAR_BREMSSTRAHLUNG enabled, the material is sliced so that only the elastic-scattering probability per slice stays below PLIMIT; the recoil probability per slice has no bound. When it exceeds one, every electron receives exactly one recoil per slice instead of a Poisson-distributed number. For electrons of momentum 20 mₑc crossing 1 m of dilute hydrogen with 2.500 expected recoils each, the model's own rates leave exp(−2.500) = 8.208% of electrons without energy loss; Elegant leaves none at the default PLIMIT, and the expected fraction once PLIMIT forces 377 slices. At the default PLIMIT, saturation needs momenta below 66.55 mₑc in hydrogen.

title: MATTER converts between mass and atom density with the proton mass
summary: With PRESSURE, TEMPERATURE and MULTIPLICITY, MATTER computes gas density using the proton mass m_p instead of the atomic mass unit u. ENERGY_DECAY and bremsstrahlung rates are consequently 0.7293% too large, and single-scattering and recoil rates, which also use a rounded u, are 0.7316% too large; with RHO supplied directly, the latter rates are 0.002344% too large. For nitrogen at 100 Pa and 300 K over 10 m, the fractional energy loss is 2.978×10⁻⁵ instead of 2.956×10⁻⁵, as an independent ideal-gas atom-density calculation shows. Forced multiple scattering converts RHO to atom density with m_p, making its angles 0.3626% too small; pressure input gives correct angles.

title: ENERGY_STRAGGLE shifts the mean energy loss and narrows its stated spread
summary: With ENERGY_DECAY=1 and ENERGY_STRAGGLE=1, MATTER multiplies each electron's exponential energy loss by 1 + 0.5·N(0, 1), with N(0, 1) a standard normal deviate, and redraws whenever the loss would be negative. title: ibsEmittance stops the equilibrium emittance at ε₀/(1+κ) when τx > τy and reports convergence
summary: ibsEmittance, run for equilibrium emittances at coupling ratio κ = εy/εx, never returns a horizontal emittance below ε₀/(1+κ), with ε₀ the uncoupled natural emittance. When the horizontal damping time τx exceeds the vertical τy (horizontal damping partition Jx < 1) and IBS is weak, the radiation–IBS balance the program solves has its root below that bound, at ε₀/(1+κτx/τy) without IBS; the program returns the bound and reports "Emittance converged". For a 3 GeV, 288.0 m ring with Jx = 0.9634, κ = 0.1 and 1 nC, it returns 48.96 nm versus 48.79 nm, 0.3408% high; the transverse balance misses zero by 0.3408% of its excitation term. This lower-bound obstruction is absent for weak IBS when τx ≤ τy.

title: IBSCATTER uses the electron's classical radius and mass for every species
summary: After change_particle selects a muon, a proton or a custom species, IBSCATTER computes its intrabeam-scattering growth rates with the electron's classical radius and mass, and so reports and applies the electron rates of the same beam. At fixed velocity, geometric phase space and particle count, the Bjorken–Mtingwa rate scales as r_c² ln Λ, with r_c the classical radius and ln Λ the Coulomb logarithm; for protons this is 4.106×10⁻⁷ of the electron rate. For a 1 nC beam at βγ = 30, the element gives protons a longitudinal rate of 8.067 s⁻¹, 2.436×10⁶ times the correct 3.312×10⁻⁶ s⁻¹. The IBS computed by moments_output is a separate calculation that uses the species' classical radius.

title: moments_output IBS Coulomb logarithm mixes electron-unit momenta with the species mass
summary: After change_particle selects a muon or a custom heavy species, moments_output with ibs_iterations forms the Coulomb logarithm ln Λ of its intrabeam-scattering (IBS) diffusion from momentum spreads in electron units but a classical minimum impact parameter with the species mass M, which inflates that cutoff by (M/mₑ)². Where it exceeds the other cutoff, ln Λ and the IBS diffusion, proportional to it, are too small. The correct value follows from Kubo and Oide's cutoffs in physical units on the same beam moments. In a radiating test ring at normalized momentum βγ = 1200 with 1 pC, ln Λ is 12.76–18.63% low for muons and 86.64–95.11% low for antiprotons, a custom species. Electrons and positrons are not affected.

title: Touschek scattering rates use the electron's classical radius for every species

title: moments_output IBS uses a negative particle count for positrons and protons
summary: After change_particle selects positrons or protons, moments_output with ibs_iterations divides the bunch charge by Elegant's internal particle charge, negative for these species, so its intrabeam-scattering (IBS) calculation uses a negative particle count. title: touschek_scatter Monte Carlo rate does not converge when the momentum aperture lies inside the sampled energy spread
summary: touschek_scatter samples the incoming beam out to distribution_cutoff (3 by default) times the rms energy spread σδ and counts every outgoing particle beyond the momentum aperture δm, including particles that were already beyond it. When δm lies inside the sampled spread, nearly forward collisions of those particles, whose Møller cross section is limited only by the sampled angle range, dominate: the Monte Carlo rate SLocalRate grows with n_simulated instead of converging, and a few particles carry the loss weights. With δm = 0.5σδ, SLocalRate is 9.372×10¹², 2.687×10¹³ and 1.395×10¹⁴ s⁻¹ for 2×10⁴, 2×10⁵ and 2×10⁶ samples, against 1.030×10¹⁰ s⁻¹ from Piwinski's formula. With δm = 31.25σδ and 2×10⁶ samples, the rate is 1.748% below Piwinski's.

title: moments_output IBS rotates the coupled diffusion tensor with transposed eigenvectors
summary: With ibs_iterations, moments_output rotates each element's intrabeam-scattering (IBS) diffusion out of the principal axes of the beam-frame momentum covariance with the transposed eigenvector matrix, so a momentum ellipsoid tilted by φ gets diffusion tilted by −φ. A ROTATE pair around a drift changes no physics, and the Kubo–Oide diffusion turns with the beam, so the equilibrium must not change. In a 524.8 m ring at 1.5 GeV/c with 1 nC, wrapping every drift in ±45° ROTATE pairs changes the IBS mode emittance e₂ from 21.00 to 20.77 pm (−1.086%) and e₁ by +0.1601%. Without rotated frames this weakly coupled ring is off by under 10⁻⁵, and beams with a diagonal momentum covariance are unaffected.

title: touschek_scatter converts normalized emittance with γ instead of βγ
summary: When normalized transverse emittances are supplied to touschek_scatter at constant energy, their conversion uses the Lorentz factor γ instead of βγ, where β is speed divided by the speed of light. title: SDDS moment accumulation discards the earlier batches
summary: The SDDS routines `accumulateMoments` and `accumulateWeightedMoments` return the mean, rms and standard deviation of data supplied in batches (first call with reset = 1, later calls with reset = 0), but in their default single-thread form they do not combine the batches. For the values 2, 4, 8, 10 supplied as [2, 4] then [8, 10], the mean is 6, the rms √46 = 6.782 and the sample standard deviation √(40/3) = 3.651, as one call over all four values gives. The unweighted routine returns a mean of 4.5 (the last batch's sum over the total count) and the unit-weight routine returns 9 (the last batch's mean).

title: The manual's bunch-input example assigns particle IDs 2001–3000 to bunch 1 instead of bunch 2
summary: The manual says that with `IDSlotsPerBunch` S the bunch of particle ID I is ⌊(I − 1)/S⌋, then illustrates this for S = 1000 with IDs 1 to 1000 in bunch 0 and IDs 2001 to 3000 in bunch 1. The formula, which the code implements, puts IDs 1001 to 2000 in bunch 1 and IDs 2001 to 3000 in bunch 2. A user who follows the example, leaving out IDs 1001 to 2000, and selects bunch 1 of a transverse wake gets no kick on any particle; in the test, the 1.252×10⁻⁷ rad kick that the example implies for particle 3000 appears only when bunch 2 is selected.
